author: Magnolia State News
title: Meridian man sentenced to over 15 years for fentanyl possession
text:
Patrick Lemon Acting United States Attorney for the Southern District of Mississippi | Department of Justice
Patrick Lemon Acting United States Attorney for the Southern District of Mississippi | Department of Justice
A Meridian, Mississippi man has been sentenced to over 15 years in prison for drug and firearm charges. Timothy Lavelle Cole, aged 47, received a 188-month sentence on June 17th for possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person.
Court documents revealed that the East Mississippi Drug Task Force conducted two controlled methamphetamine purchases from Cole at his home in April 2024. Following these transactions, agents executed a search warrant at the residence. The search uncovered various controlled substances, distribution-related items, and a firearm. Among the substances found was 101.4 grams of fentanyl. Due to prior convictions for controlled substance offenses, Cole was classified as a career offender under sentencing guidelines. He pleaded guilty to the charges on February 11, 2025.
The announcement was made by Acting U.S. Attorney Patrick A. Lemon of the Southern District of Mississippi and ATF Special Agent in Charge Joshua Jackson.
The case was investigated by the ATF and the East Mississippi Drug Task Force, with Assistant U.S. Attorney Samuel Goff prosecuting.
This investigation was part of Operation Take Back America led by the Mississippi Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF). These task forces were established under President Trump's Executive Order 14159 aimed at protecting against illegal immigration and dismantling cartels and transnational criminal organizations.
